claims.judged_criticism: checked on a 3-macro-state reduction, not the general 2-basin landscape with continuous distributions
claims.exact_statement: Fix eps>0 and work in the large-K regime (Eq 5). Under Assumption 2.1 (i,iii), there exists a constant rho_eps in (0,1) such that m_{t+1} <= rho_eps * m_t for all t. Hence m_t <= rho_eps^t m_0 -> 0 and therefore a_t + b_t -> 1.
claims.quantifiers: FOR ALL landscapes (r1,r2,eps) satisfying Assumption 2.1(i,iii) and FOR ALL admissible p_0, THERE EXISTS rho_eps in (0,1) such that FOR ALL t>=0: m_{t+1} <= rho_eps*m_t.
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: 2.1(i) bounded rewards
2.1(iii) outside gap delta>0 for both rewards on X\S_eps
2.1(iii) cross-reward gaps Delta_1,Delta_2>0
2.1(ii) is also audited even though the lemma cites only (i,iii)
claims.falsification_condition: Exhibit a landscape and p_0 satisfying every audited clause of Assumption 2.1 for which sup_t m_{t+1}/m_t >= 1. Because rho_eps is existentially quantified BEFORE the universal over t, a single step with m_{t+1} > m_t suffices.
claims.verification_condition: For the appendix form: derive m_{t+1} <= rho_eps*m_t from Assumption B.4 symbolically, and confirm geometric decay numerically on general continuous landscapes on which B.4 is measured to hold.
must_not_count_as_evidence: monotone decrease of m_t without a uniform rho<1
decay observed only on the plateau 3-state reduction
a formula-derived rho used as its own evidence

claims.anchor: Lemma 3.5 (Section 3.3); appendix Lemma B.6. Interval endpoints from Lemma 3.4 / B.5
claims.judged_criticism: the general Lemma 5 claim about bounded leakage in arbitrary 2-basin landscapes is only checked on the simplified instance
claims.exact_statement: Fix eps>0, large-K regime. Assume Assumption 2.1 and the decay conclusion of Lemma 3.3. Suppose q in (kappa_1, 1-kappa_2). Then there exist c_eps>0 and t_0 such that for all t>=t_0: max{0,(q-kappa_1)/(1-kappa_1)} - c_eps*m_t <= a_t <= min{1, q/(1-kappa_2)} + c_eps*m_t. In particular there exists eta>0 such that eta <= a_t <= 1-eta for all t>=t_0.
claims.quantifiers: FOR ALL landscapes satisfying Assumption 2.1 with m_t->0 and q in (kappa_1,1-kappa_2), THERE EXISTS eta>0 and t_0 such that FOR ALL t>=t_0: eta <= a_t <= 1-eta.
claims.secondary_statement_under_test: the specific interval endpoints (q-kappa_1)/(1-kappa_1) and q/(1-kappa_2)
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: all of Assumption 2.1
m_t -> 0 (the decay conclusion is a HYPOTHESIS here, so it may be imposed rather than derived)
kappa_1 < q < 1 - kappa_2
claims.falsification_condition: A landscape satisfying every clause with m_t->0 and q strictly inside (kappa_1,1-kappa_2) on which a_t -> 0 or a_t -> 1.
claims.verification_condition: A symbolic derivation of a strictly positive lower bound on liminf a_t and a strictly-below-one upper bound on limsup a_t, valid for all landscapes in the class, plus large-scale numerical corroboration on non-plateau continuous landscapes with adversarial parameter search.
must_not_count_as_evidence: a_inf near q on a single instance
plateau-only tests, which make basin conditionals invariant by construction and hide the eps dependence

claims.judged_criticism: a special-case identity on a 3-state system, not the general variance lower bound for arbitrary 2-basin mixtures
claims.exact_statement: Assume the setting of Theorem 3.3 and a_inf in (0,1). Then Var_{p_t}[r_i] -> Var_{p_inf}[r_i], and Var_{p_inf}[r_i] contains an explicit inter-basin term a_inf(1-a_inf)(mu_{i,1}-mu_{i,2})^2 where mu_{i,j} := E_{p_{inf,j}}[r_i]. Under basin separation this yields Var_{p_inf}[r_i] >= a_inf(1-a_inf)*max{Delta_i - 2eps, 0}^2.
claims.quantifiers: FOR ALL two-basin limit mixtures p_inf = a P1 + (1-a) P2 with a in (0,1), P_i supported on S_{i,eps}, and separation as in Assumption B.5, FOR EACH i in {1,2}: Var_{p_inf}[r_i] >= a(1-a)max{Delta_i-2eps,0}^2.
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: S_{1,eps} and S_{2,eps} disjoint
a_inf strictly inside (0,1)
separation: r_1 <= r_1*-Delta_1+eps on S_2 and r_2 <= r_2*-Delta_2+eps on S_1
bounded rewards
claims.falsification_condition: A conforming mixture with Var_{p_inf}[r_i] < a(1-a)max{Delta_i-2eps,0}^2 for some i.
claims.verification_condition: Symbolic reconstruction of the law-of-total-variance decomposition plus the two basin-mean bounds, giving the inequality for symbolic a, Delta_i, eps; and exhaustive/randomised numerical verification over general non-plateau continuous within-basin shapes.
must_not_count_as_evidence: the plateau equality Var = a(1-a)Delta^2, which is one point of the domain
checking only i=1 or only symmetric landscapes

claims.anchor: Theorem 3.7 (Section 3.3); appendix Theorem B.7; Corollary 3.8 / B.8
claims.judged_criticism: checks a calculus fact on a simplified 1-D grid; does not verify that the limiting distribution FROM pluralistic curation coincides with the Nash bargaining solution
claims.exact_statement: Let P1,P2 be fixed distributions on S_{1,eps},S_{2,eps}; p_alpha := alpha P1 + (1-alpha) P2; u_i(p) := E_p[r_i]; d_1 := u_1(P2); d_2 := u_2(P1). Assume u_1(P1)>u_1(P2) and u_2(P2)>u_2(P1). Then the weighted Nash product (u_1(p_alpha)-d_1)^q (u_2(p_alpha)-d_2)^{1-q} is uniquely maximized over alpha in [0,1] at alpha* = q. Corollary 3.8: in the plateau hard-separation regime the limiting distribution of the retraining dynamics IS that Nash point p_q.
claims.quantifiers: FOR ALL q in (0,1) and FOR ALL P1,P2,r1,r2 with strictly positive bargaining gains: argmax over the CONTINUUM alpha in [0,1] is exactly q, and the maximizer is unique.
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: strictly positive gains u_1(P1)-u_1(P2) > 0 and u_2(P2)-u_2(P1) > 0
P_i supported on the respective basins
for the Corollary: plateau structure (B.6) and vanishing leakage
claims.falsification_condition: Either a conforming instance whose Nash maximizer differs from q, or a plateau hard-separation dynamics whose limit a_inf does not converge to the Nash maximizer.
claims.verification_condition: A symbolic proof certificate over the continuum (derivative factorisation, strict log-concavity, endpoint values) valid for symbolic q -- NOT a grid search -- AND separately running the curation dynamics to convergence and comparing a_inf to the independently computed Nash argmax.
must_not_count_as_evidence: a finite grid maximisation, which cannot establish a claim about a continuum
verifying the calculus fact while skipping the dynamics-coincidence half of the claim

claims.judged_criticism: no flow-model training, no entropy/diversity measurements, no experimental data
claims.exact_statement: CIFAR-10 flow-model retraining experiments show curation with balanced multi-reward preferences sustains higher entropy and diversity than single-reward curation across recursive retraining generations.
claims.quantifiers: A directional (comparative) empirical claim: across recursive retraining generations t=1..T, balanced multi-preference curation yields higher class entropy and higher diversity proxies than single-reward curation.
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: a real generative model trained by OT-CFM on real CIFAR-10
reward derived from a real image classifier's class probabilities, r = gamma * pi_i(x)
K-BT discrete-choice curation with the paper's keep ratio
recursive retraining over multiple generations with the metrics measured per generation
claims.falsification_condition: Balanced multi-preference curation does NOT sustain higher entropy/diversity than single-reward curation, with the difference resolved beyond seed noise.
claims.verification_condition: The directional comparison holds with non-overlapping seed-level uncertainty, in a run implementing OT-CFM, real CIFAR-10 and a real classifier reward. Sample counts / model size / resolution may be downscaled for CPU, and any downscaling must be stated explicitly next to the result.
must_not_count_as_evidence: a closed-form 2-basin surrogate presented as the CIFAR-10 experiment
substituting a non-flow generative model for OT-CFM

claims.judged_criticism: a simplified proxy: no language model training, no real text generation
claims.exact_statement: Text-domain experiments confirm that curation under two competing length-based reward preferences sustains entropy over recursive retraining, consistent with the two-basin theory. Larger conflict distance d = |T_A - T_B| leads to higher sustained entropy of the generated length distribution H(L).
claims.quantifiers: Across N=20 recursive rounds, H(L) is sustained (does not collapse) under balanced two-preference curation, and sustained H(L) increases with conflict distance d.
assumptions_that_must_hold_in_any_test: an actual autoregressive language model, fine-tuned each round on its own curated generations
the paper's architecture: 6 layers, 6 heads, dim 384, GPT-2 vocab 50257
WikiText-2 seed pool of 1000 sequences
reward R(y;T) = -|L(y)-T| on word count, BT selection with tau=0.5, q=0.5
20 rounds, 200 curated per round, AdamW lr 5e-5, 2 epochs/round, batch 8
nucleus sampling at temperature 0.8 for the 200 new samples per round
H(L) = discrete entropy of the generated length distribution
claims.falsification_condition: H(L) collapses toward 0 under balanced two-preference curation, or sustained H(L) does not increase with d, beyond seed noise.
claims.verification_condition: Real LM fine-tuning loop as specified, H(L) per round, multiple seeds, single-reward negative control that DOES collapse.
must_not_count_as_evidence: a 2-basin closed-form entropy calculation with no language model
entropy of a hand-built length distribution rather than of model generations
